extDescription.message: See which trackers a page contacts and what each one did. Block trackers and ads with one click. Lens itself sends nothing.

Requests by scripts running in the page itself, including those added by other scripts, count as the page.

guideOpen.message: How to browse with less tracking

cleanOn.message: Blocking trackers is on ($1): your browser stops them before they go out.

cleanExplain.message: Off by default. When on, your browser stops third-party requests to the tracking services of our list before they go out, using its own blocking rules: Lens does not read or change those requests. Lens keeps counting what tried and what was stopped.

cleanModeVerified.message: Block the verified list ($1 services checked one by one; fewer mistakes)

cleanModeFull.message: Block the full list ($1 services, including entries not verified one by one)

cleanParams.message: Remove tracking parameters (gclid, fbclid, utm_…) from the address of pages you open

cleanWarn.message: Our list is small: this is not complete protection, and a dedicated blocker stops far more. Blocking can break parts of some sites; pause it for a site from the panel.

copiedAll.message: The whole report was copied: paste it wherever you want.

cleanModeExtended.message: Extended: our full list plus the domain rules of EasyPrivacy ($1 domains, by The EasyList authors); in Firefox, also trackers disguised as the site itself

quickTurnOff.message: On. Press to turn off (the page reloads).

quickTurnOn.message: Off. Press to turn on (the page reloads).

quickLearnTitleOff.message: Off. Press to let Lens learn trackers that are on no list from what they do (see Settings).

quickLearnTitleOn.message: On. Press to stop learning (what was learned is kept until you forget it in Settings).

learnTitle.message: Learn trackers from what they do (optional)

learnExplain.message: Off by default. When on, Lens notes third parties that are on no list but behave like trackers: they receive a cookie that looks like an identifier, or their script reads a canvas (a fingerprinting technique). One seen doing so on $1 different sites is learned. With "Block trackers" on, a learned one that read a canvas is blocked; one learned from its cookies alone keeps loading but loses its cookies, so shared logins and images keep working. Lens never keeps the names of the sites: only a short scrambled code for each, dropped once the tracker is learned.

learnCounts.message: Learned: $1 · being watched (seen on fewer sites): $2

learnNote.message: An indication, not a verdict: some services use such cookies for other reasons. Code servers, sign-in, payments, captchas and video players are never learned. If a site breaks, pause blocking there or forget the domain here.

learnHereBlocked.message: Learned by Lens from their behaviour (on no list), blocked here ($1): $2

learnHereStripped.message: Learned by Lens from their cookies (on no list), cookies removed here ($1): $2

learnHereOpen.message: Learned by Lens from their behaviour (on no list), not blocked because blocking is off or paused ($1): $2

autoRejectNote.message: Off by default. When on, Lens presses the reject button of a cookie banner as it appears (known tools such as OneTrust, Didomi, Cookiebot or Quantcast, and buttons labelled exactly as a refusal next to text about cookies) and shows a small notice in the page. It never accepts and never chooses a paid option: where the only refusal is a subscription, it tells you and does not answer. Banners whose refusal is hidden behind a settings step are left to you. Your own banner test needs this off.

noticeRejected.message: Lens rejected cookies for you on this site ($1).

noticePayOrAccept.message: This site only lets you refuse by paying ($1): Lens did not answer for you. With Block trackers on, accepting lets far fewer trackers through.

noticeNoReject.message: Lens found no reject button on this cookie banner ($1): please answer it yourself.

glanceAutoRejected.message: Lens rejected the cookie banner for you ($1).

glanceAutoNoReject.message: Lens found no reject button on the banner ($1): answer it yourself.

cleanAds.message: Block ads and hide the empty space they leave (EasyList, by The EasyList authors)

cleanAdsNote.message: Works with any of the options above, also with tracker blocking off. Ad requests are stopped by your browser's own rules, and the slots are hidden with a style sheet the browser adds to each page: Lens does not read or change the page. Some sites ask you to turn off ad blocking; pause clean mode there from the panel.

adsOn.message: Ads are blocked here with EasyList, and their empty slots hidden.

Cookie banners, subscription walls, sign-in (Google, Apple), payments (Stripe, PayPal), captchas and YouTube or Vimeo videos are allowed

When something is missing, open the panel on that site: it lists the other sites that were stopped, each with an "Allow on this site" button, or pause blocking there.

cloakedTitle.message: Disguised as part of this site

cloakedNote.message: These addresses look like the site's own, but their name points to a tracking company's servers (CNAME cloaking), so blockers that only look at the address miss them. Found by resolving names, which only Firefox allows extensions to do; companies from AdGuard's cname-trackers list.
